title: The Morgan Library presents 'Rembrandt's Lions', exploring exile and migration in 17th-century Amsterdam
summary: The Morgan Library & Museum presents Rembrandt's Lions: Art and Exile in the Dutch Republic, an exhibition that brings together, for the first time, a remarkable group of drawings, etchings, and paintings highlighting the often overlooked but formative presence of migrants, immigrants, exiles, and refugees in the world and work of Rembrandt Harmenszoon van Rijn (1606–1669). The exhibition particularly focuses on stories of diaspora, or dispersed communities, that figure prominently in many of his etchings, offering a new perspective on the effects of migration on seventeenth-century life. Today, Rembrandt is seen as the quintessential Dutch artist, yet in his day the Dutch Republic was newly formed, and what it meant to be Dutch was still being defined. On view from October 23, 2026, through January 31, 2027, this exhibition illuminates a new interpretation of the artist and the world he inhabited. title: Olney Gleason presents 'Tina Barney: Fashion', bridging editorial photography and fine art
summary: Olney Gleason announces Tina Barney: Fashion, a solo exhibition of work by American photographer Tina Barney (b. 1945), on view at 297 Tenth Avenue, New York, from October 24 through November 14, 2026. The exhibition brings together nearly four decades of Barney’s major editorial commissions and campaigns for global fashion brands, between the late 1980s and the present—works that continue to expand the range of the artist’s photography practice. Tina Barney: Fashion is presented concurrently with the publication of the comprehensive monograph of the same title (Aperture, 2026). It marks Barney’s first New York exhibition to follow Family Ties, the major touring retrospective organized by the Jeu de Paume, Paris, in 2024-2025. Fashion has played a central role in Barney’s life from a young age: the artist’s mother, Lillian Fox, was a former model whose sense of style deeply inspired Barney. title: Christie's to offer an exceptionally rare Patek Philippe Dual Time Ref. 3452/1 as a highlight of December Luxury Week
summary: An exceptionally rare Patek Philippe, designed by master watchmaker Louis Cottier and never-before-seen by the public, is being offered by Christie's as a centerpiece of The Important Watches auction during Luxury Week in New York in December. The Patek Philippe Dual Time Reference 3452/1 (estimate $800,000 to $1.6 million) is one of only seven unique timepieces with this reference conceived by legendary watchmaker Cottier. This is the first example of the reference to appear on the market in two decades, and the last of the seven examples to be unveiled. The 18K white and yellow gold watch is headed to market for the first time, 65 years after leaving the Patek Philippe workshops. title: Design Week Lagos unveils '180 New Ideas' and plans for Design Museum Africa
summary: Design Week Lagos 2026 was officially inaugurated at the National Theatre in Lagos on 22 October with the 180 New Ideas exhibition and IDEA Honours awards ceremony. Design Week Lagos runs until 25 October 2026 at the National Theatre Lagos and venues around the city. Making a New Africa: From Material to Market is the theme running through Design Week Lagos 2026, which features a programme exploring how African design can move beyond international recognition to shape manufacturing, commerce and industrial development. Centred on the question of what Africa will make next, the festival positions Lagos as an increasingly significant destination for global design, creative exchange and innovation. Leading the curatorial programme of Design Week Lagos 2026 is Norman Teague, founder of Chicago-based Norman Teague Design Studios. Teague worked closely with curators Nana Biamah-Ofosu, Ousmane Mbaye and Júlio Rafael across the Anglophone, Francophone and Lusophone perspectives. At the heart o

title: MNBAQ opens $84M Espace Riopelle - Michael Audain Pavilion dedicated to Jean Paul Riopelle
summary: The Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec (MNBAQ) began a new chapter with the grand opening of the Espace Riopelle – Michael Audain Pavilion . The new building is a lasting tribute from the centennial celebrations for artist Jean Paul Riopelle (1923–2002), honouring the work of one of the most influential Québec and Canadian artists of the 20th century. Designed by multi -award-winning Québec firm Les architectes FABG , this three storey, over 5,600 m² building is the largest space entirely dedicated to a Canadian artist . The $84M project is the result of a major partnership between the Government of Québec, the City of Québec, and the philanthropic community. It is intended to promote and preserve the artistic legacy of the internationally renowned painter, sculptor, and lithographer. This building on the historic Plains of Abraham is the fourth in the museum complex. The visitor experience extends both indoors and out: the interior

title: Santiago Mostyn appointed curator of Gteborg International Biennial for Contemporary Art 14th edition
summary: Göteborg International Biennial for Contemporary Art (GIBCA) is delighted to announce the appointment of Santiago Mostyn as curator of the 14th edition of the project, taking place at art centres and collaborative venues throughout Gothenburg, from September 4–November 21, 2027. Santiago Mostyn is an artist based in Stockholm who works within film, installation, and performance. His practice can be viewed as an ongoing visual research framework in which non-aligned histories and personal memory intersect. Mostyn grew up in Trinidad and Zimbabwe, received his BA from Yale University, and was the 2024–25 Logie Fellow at Harvard Radcliffe Institute. Mostyn curated, together with Joa Ljungberg, The Moderna Exhibition: With the Future Behind Us (2018), a comprehensive presentation of artists connected to the Swedish art scene that reckoned with questions of cultural and spiritual identity. title: CIMAM raises concerns over removal of artworks and historical objects from Colombia's National Museum
summary: The International Committee for Museums and Collections of Modern Art (CIMAM) has expressed serious concern over the removal of artworks, photographs, documents and historical objects from the permanent displays of the Museo Nacional de Colombia, warning that the decision could undermine public access to the country's history and threaten the professional independence of museum institutions. In a statement issued by its Museum Watch initiative, CIMAM criticized the removal of at least 30 objects on October 15, 2026, following instructions from Colombia's Ministry of Cultures, Arts and Knowledges. The materials documented significant chapters in the country's recent history, including feminist and LGBTQ+ movements, political violence, the constitutional process of 1991 and the peace agreement signed in 2016. title: American Modernism from the Charles Butt Collection opens at the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston
summary: American Modernism from the Charles Butt Collection is the first exhibition organized from the collection of philanthropist and Texas native Charles Butt. Featuring over 80 works of art by such icons as Stuart Davis, Georgia O'Keeffe, Jacob Lawrence, Thomas Hart Benton, Jackson Pollock, Joan Mitchell and Andrew Wyeth, as well as Texas artists like Everett Gee Jackson and Mary Bonner, the exhibition reflects and recontextualizes the multifold histories of American art by sharing Butt's perspective on American creativity and presenting his collection to the public for the first time. The exhibition is on view at the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston from October 25, 2026 through January 18, 2027. "Charles Butt is widely known in Texas for his philanthropy and abiding commitment to education," comments Gary Tinterow, director and Margaret Alkek Williams chair of the MFAH. title: Eliyah Mesayer expands her imaginary state 'Illiyeen' in new Copenhagen exhibition
summary: In Letters from a Huntress, Eliyah Mesayer’s first solo exhibition with NILS STÆRK, the artist continues her ongoing project Illiyeen, an imaginary state. Conceived as both a poetic nation and a conceptual manifestation, Illiyeen is brought into being through stories, rituals, and symbols. It has its own flag, uniforms, postal service, national anthem, and manifest, offering a place for those who exist between borders – between reality and fiction, politics and poetry. Within the imagined geography of Illiyeen, the huntress appears as a traveler, messenger, and possible guardian. Her precise role remains unresolved, allowing her to move between different identities and meanings throughout the exhibition. Through this figure, Mesayer extends her ongoing exploration of belonging, nationhood, statelessness, movement, and the idea of home into a more intimate and poetic register. title: Michelangelo Pistoletto takes over Galleria Continua's Marais space
summary: Galleria Continua is presenting, in its Marais exhibition space, in the heart of Paris, the solo exhibition of Michelangelo Pistoletto, Avant et après l’Arte Povera. Michelangelo Pistoletto is not only an Arte Povera artist, but one of the protagonists of the movement that Germano Celant theorised and defined in 1967. Arte Povera represents only one stage within a practice that now spans seventy years. Pistoletto’s artistic path began earlier and, above all, has continued to develop along a trajectory of its own. To tie him exclusively to Arte Povera would be to reduce the complexity and breadth of a practice that has continually transformed the relationship between art, the individual and society. In Pistoletto’s artistic history, there is a before and an after. These are not two separate moments, but successive phases of a practice that, through radical transformations, has laid the foundations of what is now his oeuvre. title: $25M real gemstone Marvel Infinity Gauntlet going to auction for first time
summary: Julien’s Auctions and East Continental Gems today announced that the Marvel Infinity Gauntlet replica — a one-of-one piece set with six exceptional gems, each representing one of the Infinity Stones — will be offered at auction. This December in Abu Dhabi, the 1-of-1 Infinity Gauntlet will be a headline lot of Julien’s Celebrity & Culture Experience during the Pop Culture Legends Evening Sale on December 8, 2026 at Rosewood Abu Dhabi on Al Maryah Island. The Gauntlet was unveiled at San Diego Comic-Con in 2022 and offered for sale at $25 million. The launch and $25 million figure were covered at the time, as reported by various financial news outlets. The Infinity Gauntlet is among the most recognized objects in modern popular culture, following decades of Marvel storytelling across Marvel Comics and Marvel Studios’ films. title: The Cleveland Museum of Art commissions new site-specific work by Teresita Fernández
summary: The Cleveland Museum of Art announced today the acquisition of Soil Horizon(Cleveland), a site-specific commissioned work by acclaimed artist Teresita Fernández, whose work is characterized by an expansive rethinking of what constitutes landscape. Comprising two large-scale glazed ceramic wall murals, the work will be installed in the Jane and Jon Outcalt Family Concourse, connecting the museum’s Horace Kelley Art Foundation North Lobby with the Ames Family Atrium, beginning in February 2027. The commission completes the transformation of the CMA’s Horace Kelley Art Foundation North Lobby and adjoining spaces, undertaken in 2024 to enhance the visitor experience while respecting the distinctive architecture of Marcel Breuer. title: Fifty artists examine the unfamiliar in new collection survey at Espoo Museum of Modern Art
summary: What can the unfamiliar reveal about ourselves and our surroundings? Alien in Me, a new presentation of Saastamoinen Foundation Art Collection at EMMA – Espoo Museum of Modern Art, brings together works by over 50 artists to explore experiences of alienation and otherness in a world undergoing constant transformation. Curated by EMMA Director Krist Gruijthuijsen, the exhibition includes Finnish and international names such as Eija-Liisa Ahtila, Louise Bourgeois, Peter Hujar, Isaac Julien, Nnena Kalu, Cindy Sherman, Jenna Sutela and Gillian Wearing. The exhibition opens on October 23, 2026, marking 20 years of collaboration between EMMA and its founding partner, Saastamoinen Foundation. Alien in Me refers to the unfamiliar both within ourselves and in the world around us.

title: Philadelphia Museum of Art announces transformative $20 million gift
summary: The Philadelphia Museum of Art (PMA) today announced a $20 million gift from Lois G. and Julian A. Brodsky to establish the new Lois G. and Julian A. Brodsky Learning and Engagement Center (Brodsky Center). Their commitment is among the largest in the museum’s history and will transform the north wing into a dedicated space for advancing the museum’s educational mission. The Brodsky Center is the PMA’s first major capital project since the Core Project, Frank Gehry’s landmark four-year interior renovation and expansion, which reopened to the public in May 2021. The Brodsky Center will expand the museum’s reach to students, children, and families while welcoming audiences of all ages into inclusive and engaging spaces. title: Irini Papadimitriou appointed Artistic Director of the 14th Seoul Mediacity Biennale
summary: The Seoul Museum of Art (SeMA) has appointed Irini Papadimitriou as Artistic Director of the 14th Seoul Mediacity Biennale, scheduled to open in August 2027. Currently serving as Director of Exhibitions at Diriyah Art Futures in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, Papadimitriou is a curator whose practice critically examines the relationships between art, technology, and society. Her previous roles include positions at the Victoria and Albert Museum (V&A) and FutureEverything in the United Kingdom. Originally launched with the exhibition SEOUL in MEDIA in 1996, the Seoul Mediacity Biennale has established itself over the past 30 years as one of Seoul’s leading international art events. Grounded in the distinctive urban context of Seoul and its rapidly changing media environment, the Biennale has moved beyond a purely technological understanding of media

title: Minja Gu explores migration, dietary restrictions, and global ethics at Alt Space LOOP
summary: Reproductive labour moves across national borders. Korea, once subjected to colonial rule, now occupies a quasi-imperial position, drawing on resources, labour and care from the Global South. In Yangpyeong in 2018, Minja Gu met Lusi Sapitri, an Indonesian marriage migrant. Sapitri recounted how she had once eaten jajang-myeon (noodles in black bean sauce) without knowing it was made with pork. In her Korean household she is expected to cook Korean food, with pork, as part of her familial duty. She is expected to feed the family, yet has no say in setting the rules of the table. Middle Ground begins with a proposition that reverses this asymmetry. If everyone in the world sat at one table, bringing even taboos they no longer practised, what could they eat together? title: Eva Fabbris is the new Artistic Director of Fondazione Società delle Api
summary: The Fondazione Società delle Api announces the appointment of Eva Fabbris as Artistic Director. Already a member of the Advisory Board since its inception, Fabbris takes on a role that marks a new phase in the institutional development of Società delle Api, strengthening its curatorial structure while preserving the collective dimension that has characterized the Foundation. Her directorship will help give curatorial form to an already collective approach, which involves the role of artists and curators in shaping the cultural programme. The appointment comes at a particularly vibrant moment for the Foundation. With the opening of its Roman space at via Gregoriana 40 on 14 February 2026, Società delle Api gave expression to its nature and mission: to welcome and bring together artists, curators and scholars, and to create the conditions for shared projects to emerge

title: Salt Galata interrogates the evolution of the factory
summary: Workplaces are among the most central yet least visible spaces of everyday life. They often remain outside the public eye as closed spaces to which there is “no admittance except on business.” Once a symbol of industrial capitalism with its chimneys rising above city centers, the factory largely lost its urban visibility after 1980, as production was reorganized on a global scale. As manufacturing facilities in city centers gave way to residential projects, shopping centers, and cultural venues, production moved to the outskirts of cities, Organized Industrial Zones, and new infrastructural geographies where logistics networks converge. Yet spaces of production extend beyond the physical boundaries of the factory; they transform the earth, everyday life, and digital space into a continuous field of work. title: New exhibition shows the lasting legacy and inspiration of John Constable for Suffolk's artists
summary: Colchester + Ipswich Museums’ (CIMS) Constable 250 – a year-long programme of exhibitions, performances and events – concludes with a very special show that showcases artworks made by members of the local community, alongside paintings by seven professional contemporary artists, all of whom have been inspired by John Constable’s legacy and indelible contribution to British painting. Constable to Contemporary will also display pictures made by the next generation of exciting young talents to be found in the area. Suffolk Artlink’s Brave Art Groups, for adults with learning disabilities, has developed a new body of mixed media works inspired by the work of Constable, while Community Hub Ipswich (CHIp Studios) has created a youth-led immersive artwork that brings to life the essence of ‘Constable Country’ through the senses.

title: Museum PARCUM presents Threading Landscapes at Park Abbey in Leuven
summary: After fifteen years of restoration, the historic monastic complex of Park Abbey in Leuven is opening fully to the public for the first time. Museum PARCUM marks this exceptional moment with Threading Landscapes: Art at Park Abbey, an ambitious exhibition featuring work by 24 contemporary artists from around the world. Nine artists have developed new projects in direct response to the abbey, its architecture, landscape, biodiversity, archives and history. This moment represents more than the completion of a restoration. It marks the beginning of a new phase. Heritage, after all, is not static, but an ongoing process of interpretation, care and meaning-making. How do we relate today to a place that carries almost nine centuries of history, while at the same time inviting us to shape its future? Museum PARCUM places this question at the heart

title: Berlin Biennale for Contemporary Art presents 14th edition Central Europe Eastern Time
summary: The 14th Berlin Biennale for Contemporary Art takes place from June 5 to September 12, 2027 at various locations across Berlin and is curated by Vasyl Cherepanyn. Under the title Central Europe Eastern Time, the 14th Berlin Biennale proposes a new reading of Berlin from the East and offers a perspective on Europe shaped by those regions, experiences, and societal realities that have long been pushed to the margins of the European narrative. The title serves as a navigation tool, an instrument of orientation, and describes a chronotope in which space (tópos) and time (chrónos) are inseparably connected. It points to how shifting political, economic, and ideological systems define today’s conditions of human coexistence. In this sense, orientation is not only a question of where we are, but also of understanding the different historical and political

title: Chassica "Chaz" Kirchhoff appointed the J. J. Medveckis Curator of Arms and Armor
summary: The Philadelphia Museum of Art announced the appointment of Dr. Chassica “Chaz” Kirchhoff as the J. J. Medveckis Curator of Arms and Armor. Kirchhoff joins the PMA from the Detroit Institute of Arts. She begins her new role on November 30, 2026. “We are delighted to welcome Chassica as the J. J. Medveckis Curator of Arms and Armor. She brings a deep knowledge of the field, and her curatorial and scholarly achievements make her ideal for the role,” said Daniel Weiss, the George D. Widener Director and CEO. “As we approach the fiftieth anniversary of Carl Otto Kretzschmar von Kienbusch’s foundational gift of the museum’s Arms and Armor collection in 2027, we are excited for Chassica to shape new exhibitions and interpretations that will commemorate this important milestone and showcase the collection’s extraordinary highlights.

title: Talbot Rice Gallery launches global three-part exhibition project 'The Rupture'
summary: The Rupture is an international collaboration bringing together the University of Edinburgh's Talbot Rice Gallery, Inside-Out Art Museum in Beijing and the Museum of Contemporary Art and Design in Manila. Conceived by Tessa Giblin and Carol Yinghua Lu, with Joselina Cruz completing the curatorial partnership, the project responds in real time to a world undergoing profound political, social and economic change, echoing Mark Carney's declaration that "we are in the midst of a rupture” in his 2026 Davos address. Curated in three episodes, The Rupture will launch at Talbot Rice Gallery in October 2026, just nine months after Davos. At a time of profound global uncertainty, The Rupture: No condition is permanent asks what it means to live through the breakdown of established systems, rules-based order and global relationships.
